Mandatory Background:

1) Understanding Formal Methods by Jean-Francois Monin - This is the absolute best for getting a grip on the breadth, concepts and sample tools for Formal Mathematics/Specification/Verification. Fire-hose of information (not a step-by-step textbook) so use this as a map for everything "Formal". The S/N ratio is very high (~250 pages only!) so use AI as your personal tutor for concepts you find difficult to understand.

Practical:

1) Software Abstractions: Logic, Language, and Analysis by Daniel Jackson - Uses "Alloy" language to teach Structural (i.e. Data) Modeling.

2) Specifying Systems: The TLA+ Language and Tools for Hardware and Software Engineers by Leslie Lamport - Uses "TLA+" language to teach Behavioural (i.e. State Machine) modeling.

There are a few more (eg. Event-B etc.) but you can get to those when you need to.
